newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Gunmen target Cameroon forces, kill two.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen target Cameroon forces, kill two.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen have killed at least two paramilitary gendarmes in attacks in Cameroon's volatile English-speaking northwest province, according to state radio.

Weekend reports on the radio said the gunmen had killed the gendarmes during a series of attacks on gendarme police posts and other public buildings on Thursday and Friday in the provincial capital Bamenda and Mbengwi, Jakari and Kumbo.
Opposition veteran John Fru Ndi blamed the government of President Paul Biya for the attacks, saying they were part of a attempt to find an excuse to postpone elections.
"He is always looking to postpone the elections due to be held in Cameroon," the Social Democratic Front leader told Africa Number One Radio station in an interview on Saturday.
The government has made no formal comment.
Cameroon is due to hold its postponed parliamentary election in May. The government has yet to announce a precise date.
The election will be the second parliamentary poll since Cameroon's sometimes turbulent transition to multi-party democracy began in 1990.
Part of the opposition boycotted the last legislative election in 1992. Biya supporters secured a majority then after allying with a minor party.

The government postponed this year's election from March after opposition party complaints that their militants had not had enough time to register. The opposition has demanded an independent national electoral commission.
Biya, who took over from independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo in 1982, faces a presidential election in October.
